in your answer.

text: Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreams) compared dream duration estimates for 5-minute and
15-minute REM periods.
Write a null hypothesis for this part of the study.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline what is meant by ‘inter-rater reliability’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one part of the procedure that improved inter-rater reliability in this study.

text: In the study by Bandura et al. (aggression), inter-rater reliability was measured.
In the study by Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans), observers counted the total number of victims
helped. The results were that 62 ‘cane’ victims and 19 ‘drunk’ victims were helped.
Draw a bar chart of these results. You must label the axes.
In a study on memory, participants had to recall a story. The researchers measured memory by
rating the accuracy of each participant’s recall of the story on a 10-point scale.
Suggest one weakness of using this scale to measure memory.
Describe laboratory experiments and field experiments, using any examples.

parts.text: Explain one strength of the case study research method.

parts.text:
Explain two weaknesses of the case study research method, using Bruce’s study as an
example.

text: Bruce is planning a case study of a famous woman known worldwide for her helpfulness.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Nola and Tim have different ideas for recording participants’ hours of sleep per night:
• Nola plans to ask participants to record this at home.
• Tim says it would be better to record this in a laboratory.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest one ethical reason why Nola’s idea is better than Tim’s idea.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest one practical reason why Nola’s idea is better than Tim’s idea, other than
avoiding the need to use a laboratory.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Suggest one practical reason why Tim’s idea is better than Nola’s idea.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Nola finds the correlation she expected, that people who sleep less argue more.
Explain why Nola cannot know whether sleeping less causes people to argue more.

text: Nola is investigating whether there is a correlation between hours of sleep and how much a
person argues. She thinks that people who sleep less may argue more. Her friend Tim is making
suggestions about her procedure.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Naomi could either be a participant observer or a non-participant observer.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest one advantage of her being a participant observer.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest one advantage of her being a non-participant observer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain the type of data Naomi is collecting.

parts.text: Situational variables could affect Naomi’s results.

Answer all questions in this section.

text: Naomi is designing an observation of helping behaviour at an entrance to a library that has a door
which is difficult to open. She intends to observe people carrying many books and will record the
gender of each person who helps to open the door.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how Brendan could conduct a study using a semi-structured interview to investigate
participants’ feelings, thoughts and actions towards other road users.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify one practical weakness/limitation with the procedure you have described in your
answer to part (a) and suggest how your study might be done differently to overcome the
problem.
Do not refer to ethics or sampling in your answer.

text: Brendan is planning to use a semi-structured interview in a study about road users. He intends to
use a sample of people who are walking (pedestrians). Brendan will investigate the pedestrians’
feelings, thoughts and actions towards other road users, e.g. other pedestrians, cyclists and drivers.
